newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia deal technical - Merita fund.
newsitem.headline: Nokia deal technical - Merita fund.

text.p: The pension fund of Finland's Merita Bank said on Thursday its sale of shares in telecoms group Nokia Oy to Merita Bank was a technical way of returning its accumulated surplus to the bank.

"The pension fund does not have the liquid assets (to give to the bank)," finance director Martti Huhtamaki told Reuters by telephone. "The net result of this transaction is that Merita got those shares without any payment."
Merita said earlier its pension fund had sold about 4.5 million K-series shares in Nokia to Merita Bank and its subsidiary Nordica Invest Oy for about 1.4 billion markka.
Of the 1.4 billion markka that the pension fund receives, 1.2 billion will go to Merita group companies next week and the fund will keep the remaining 200 million, Huhtamaki said.
"The whole result of this is that Merita Group got 1.2 billion (markka) in new free Nokia shares and got that 1.2 billion from the pension fund," he added.
He said Merita's group equity would be increased by 1.2 billion markka: in its profit and loss account the cash payment would be recorded as extraordinary income.
Clarifying a share capital hike for Nordica Invest to enable it to buy a share of the Nokia stock, Huhtamaki said the total cash injection was 575 million markka.
Of this, 115 million would go onto Nordica's equity line and 460 million to ordinary reserves.
After Thursday's transaction, he said the pension fund will still hold just over 5 million Nokia K shares.
"We still have an unrealised surplus in the fund which is more than 1.1 billion markka," he said. Asked if the fund would also seek to return this to Merita Bank, he said: "We'll see."
The deal, made possible by permission from the social and health ministry last week, stems from a legal change in 1995, he added.
